excerpt: You hold forest over seven tenths of your land, rivers that give almost all your power, and more fresh water per person than most nations on earth.
paras: You hold forest over seven tenths of your land, rivers that give almost all your power, and more fresh water per person than most nations on earth. Almost half of you are children. The task is to turn what stands and flows into services that reach every one of them.

Your partners have not looked away. In June 2026 the World Bank approved $90 million for your part of the first phase of the Douala–Bangui corridor, your road to the sea. In July 2026 the Green Climate Fund approved $69.1 million with UNICEF for water, sanitation and hygiene that can withstand the climate. France has lent €25 million to your budget and given €5.2 million to restore the Boali hydroelectric plant.

The work ahead is plain, and it is worth saying plainly. Only one in every hundred of you cooks with clean fuel, and fewer than one in five has electricity. Only six in every hundred of you have safely managed drinking water. At the last count, in 2016, fewer than nine in every hundred of your young people completed lower secondary school. Clean energy sets your Coverage today, at 1 out of 100, with water and schooling close behind. Each of them is within your reach.

Now imagine that same resolve turned toward every home in the country. Picture Perfect Central African Republic: a morning when every family cooks with clean fuel and sits down to a full table; when every tap runs clean and every home has a safe toilet; when every child walks to a school where a teacher is waiting, and reads with ease by the age of ten; when every mother lives within reach of a clinic with the lights on, and every young person finds work that pays. And no Central African falls below a decent life, because the nation has decided that none will.
quote: What stands and what flows can feed and teach every child. Let the forest and the rivers pay.
